title: The Foolish Servant (Português)
summary: A nobleman boasts of his servant's absolute, unquestioning obedience. Birbal proves that mindless obedience without common sense is dangerous. [PT]
full_text:
A proud courtier named Mirza Zahir boasted before Emperor Akbar that he possessed the finest servant in the empire: 'My servant Ghafoor never questions an order! He obeys every word literally, without a moment's hesitation!'

Birbal remarked quietly: 'Mirza Sahib, obedience without common sense is a curse, not a blessing. A servant who cannot think will eventually destroy his master.'

Zahir scoffed: 'Nonsense! A servant's only duty is to obey!'

A few days later, while Zahir was hosting a garden party for the Emperor and his courtiers, Zahir noticed his pet falcon perched on a high marble wall. Wanting to show off his servant's blind obedience, Zahir called out: 'Ghafoor! Bring that falcon down immediately! Do whatever it takes, but do not let it fly away!'

Ghafoor ran to the wall. The bird was perched twelve feet up. Seeing a heavy wooden pole nearby, Ghafoor swung it with all his might, striking the falcon directly across the head! The bird fell dead at his feet.

Ghafoor picked up the dead bird, presented it proudly to his master, and said: 'Here is the falcon, master! As you commanded, I did not let it fly away!'

Zahir turned purple with rage and embarrassment, while the entire assembly gasped in horror.

Birbal stepped forward and said gently: 'You see, Mirza Sahib? He obeyed your exact words with complete literalness! You told him to bring the falcon down and not let it fly away, but you did not instruct him to keep it alive!

'A human being must never be an unthinking machine. When choosing servants, soldiers, or counselors, value sound judgment and discernment above blind, mindless obedience.'

Zahir bowed his head in deep humility, and Akbar commended Birbal for illustrating the vital difference between mechanical obedience and true wisdom.
